subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals \u0014 next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals  next steps

Hi Emily 

Great to meet you and the Acme Data team this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call focused on long-context evaluation for your analytics reports and legal doc summarization use cases.

Key takeaways:
- Primary goal: verify summarization fidelity and truncation behavior for inputs in the 8k64k token range (most important: no factual drops on multi-section legal docs).
- Success metrics: ROUGE/ROUGE-L + targeted QA checks on entity preservation and cross-section reference correctness; tolerate small compressions but no hallucinated facts.
- Demo preference: run a 1015 sample run with your canonical doc set and our recommended models/configs, then review with your team.

Recommended models & configs (initial):
- redwood/longform-65b-8k  conservative, best summarization fidelity for 8k windows.
- redwood/rwx-13b-64k (quantized int8)  cost-effective large-window option for 64k.
- quant profiles: int8-qdq for rwx-13b-64k; bf16 for 65b where possible.

Deliverables we propose:
1) Run batch eval on 25 representative docs (mix of legal, product specs, and chat logs) with both 8k & 64k configs and provide a dashboard/report.
2) Share prompt-set we used (attached: acme_long_context_prompt_set_v1.json) and truncation samples (attached).
3) One-hour review call next week to walk results and recommended production config (canary, batching, caching).

Questions for you:
- Do we have a preferred subset of docs (PII or redacted) to use, or can we use the sample set you uploaded to the Drive link during the call?
- Any SLA/cost constraints we should keep in mind for the 64k runs? (we can estimate in the deliverable)

Proposed times for the review call: Tue 4/20 1011am PT, Wed 4/21 23pm PT. Let me know what works and Ill send a calendar invite.

Thanks  looking forward.


Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194

Attachments: acme_long_context_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_truncation_samples.csv

Thanks Marissa  really helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Cost/latency: our platform team is sensitive to inference latency at 64k windows. Can you include an estimated per-request latency and cost for the rwx-13b-64k quantized run vs the 65b-8k run? We need to weigh fidelity vs cost.
2) Data: we uploaded a redacted sample set to the Drive folder (see link you shared). Use that for the initial run if that works.
3) Procurement: looping in procurement to get ahead of any contracting questions  procurement@acme.com.

Wed 4/21 23pm PT works for us. Please send the invite.


Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of Data Platforms, Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Long-context evals  next steps

Hi Emily  quick technical notes on latency/cost estimates and what the eval will capture:

- Expected median latency (inference-only token-time) per 10k tokens:
  - rwx-13b-64k (int8-qdq): ~650900 ms per 1k tokens on an A100-class instance; 10k token document end-to-end ~6.59s token-generation time (plus overhead).
  - longform-65b-8k (bf16): ~1.21.8s per 1k tokens; large model overhead  1218s for 10k sequence if run naively.
- Cost: approximate GPU-second bucketing gives ~3045% lower GPU compute cost for rwx-13b-64k quantized runs vs bf16 65b for equivalent token output. Detailed cost breakdown will be in the report.
- Truncation behavior we will test:
  - prefix preservation: confirm the first N sections remain intact for summarization prompts.
  - cross-reference integrity: tests to ensure entity references that appear in earlier sections are resolved correctly in the summary.
  - KV cache & chunked inference: we'll run chunked inference with overlap windows to detect where factual drop occurs and quantify it.

Benchmark links (internal): https://redwood.ai/bench/long-context-acme-2027  contains past runs, token distributions, and quantization comparison charts.

Implementation note (prompt engineering): our prompt-set will include explicit 'anchor' markers to preserve section boundaries. Example prompt seed: 

--- prompt start ---
You are an assistant that must produce a concise executive summary that preserves all named entities and cross-references. Use the "SECTION:" markers below to locate references. If an entity is outside the provided context, indicate "OUT-OF-CONTEXT" rather than guessing.
--- prompt end ---

We will attach a sample runner config for you (and include the prompt-set as Marissa attached).


Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Procurement  thanks for joining the thread. For contracting we expect to propose an evaluation SOW (covering compute credits for the runs) and then discuss Dedicated vs Hosted for longer pilots. We'll share a rough SOW draft before the meeting.

If anything else comes up before Wednesday, ping me here. Looking forward.


Marissa
